fact: Example: NEVER use 'as any' type casting - it hides bugs and defeats TypeScript's type system.
recommendation: Use proper type narrowing, generics, or 'as unknown as Type' for test mocks.

fact: Using `npm install -g X 2>&1 | tail -1` to install global packages in bash scripts suppresses all output including error messages. Only the last line of output is shown, which is often the npm fund notice — not the actual error. A failing install will appear silent.
recommendation: Replace with `npm install -g X &>/dev/null || die "Failed to install X"`. This produces no output on success and a clear error message on failure via the die() function.

fact: The bash idiom `A && B || C` is an anti-pattern (SC2156/SC2015): if A succeeds but B fails, C will also execute unexpectedly. This is especially dangerous in install scripts where fallback branches run even when the primary path partially succeeded.
recommendation: Use proper if/then/else: `if A; then B; else C; fi`. Reserve `&&` for chaining on success and `||` for failure-only fallbacks, never combined in a single line.

fact: Using variables as the format string in printf causes SC2059 shellcheck warnings and is a security risk (printf injection). Example: `printf "${CYAN}text${NC}\n"` is wrong because $CYAN could contain format specifiers.
recommendation: Always use a literal format string: `printf '%s%s%s\n' "${CYAN}" "text" "${NC}"`. The format string should never contain variable expansions.

fact: Hardcoding the GitHub repo name as `solanaclawd` (missing hyphen) in URLs breaks curl installs and clones. The correct repo name is `solana-clawd` (Solizardking/solana-clawd). Two separate root causes existed: wrong org case AND wrong repo name in the one-liner.
recommendation: Always use the canonical URL: `https://github.com/Solizardking/solana-clawd`. For the curl one-liner: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solizardking/solana-clawd/main/pay.sh`. Never abbreviate or drop hyphens in repo names.

fact: Running `npm install` or `npm install -g` inside a pnpm workspace without switching to pnpm first can corrupt the lockfile, install to the wrong node_modules hoisting level, or create a package-lock.json that conflicts with pnpm-lock.yaml.
recommendation: In pnpm workspaces always use `pnpm add`, `pnpm install`, or `pnpm exec`. For global installs that are deliberately npm-global (like clawd, clawd-registry, clawd-hub, agentwallet-vault), explicitly run npm from outside the workspace context.

fact: Importing from `@solana/mpp` when the local package has not been built (`pnpm build`) will fail at runtime because the package only ships `src/` TypeScript files — there is no `dist/` from the npm registry version (0.6.0).
recommendation: Always `cd typescript/packages/mpp && pnpm build` before any code that imports from @solana/mpp. In package.json use `file:../../typescript/packages/mpp` instead of the npm registry version to ensure the local built copy is used.

fact: Exposing internal route paths, admin endpoints, auth flow internals, API keys, wallet addresses, or implementation details in public GitHub PRs, comments, or issue descriptions is a critical security violation. Any public communication from this project is a potential attack surface.
recommendation: Never include x402.wtf internal route structure, CAAP auth token shapes, wallet private keys, admin endpoints, or infrastructure hostnames in any public PR/issue/comment. Public-facing content should only describe user-facing behavior and public API surfaces.

fact: Using `cd` to navigate into a subdirectory at the start of a bash script changes the working directory for all subsequent commands. This breaks relative path assumptions if the script is called from a different directory or sourced.
recommendation: Use absolute paths or `$(dirname "$0")` to construct paths relative to the script location. Avoid naked `cd` at top-level scope — use `(cd subdir && command)` subshell for directory-scoped operations.

fact: Hardcoding Solana RPC URLs (https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com) in production code without an env-var override creates fragility. The free public RPC is heavily rate-limited and will cause silent failures in high-throughput agent scenarios.
recommendation: Always read RPC URL from environment: `process.env.SOLANA_RPC_URL ?? 'https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com'`. Ship a default only as a dev fallback. In production, use a Helius or Triton RPC URL from the .env file.

fact: Using `set -e` alone in bash scripts (without `-u` and `pipefail`) will silently swallow errors in piped commands and unset variable expansions. `pipe1 | pipe2` — if pipe1 fails, the exit code is discarded and pipe2's exit code is used.
recommendation: Always use `set -euo pipefail` at the top of every bash script. The `-o pipefail` ensures pipe failures propagate, `-u` catches unset variables, `-e` exits on error. This is the minimum safe baseline for installer scripts.

fact: Putting OpenRouter or xAI API keys in NEXT_PUBLIC_* / client-bundled env vars exposes secrets in the browser. CLAWD Bot free chat must proxy through a server route that holds OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the client only hits same-origin /api/clawd-bot or production companion endpoints.
recommendation: Server-only secrets: OPENROUTER_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, CLAWDROUTER_API_KEY. Client may know public model labels only. Reject any PR that adds NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENROUTER_API_KEY or embeds sk-or- keys in client code.

fact: Allowing arbitrary model ids on the public free-chat route enables paid OpenRouter models and surprise billing. Free companion traffic must be gated to openrouter/free or *:free only.
recommendation: Always run body.model through isOpenRouterFreeModelId before calling OpenRouter from free-chat/stream. Return 400 for paid models. Do not trust client-supplied model strings for billing-sensitive paths.
